answer: The server enforces a strictly increasing sequence number on every request inside a session, and any gap or repeat is treated as a fork. A real client never skips a number, so a session that shows two requests with the same sequence — or a jump — is evidence that the session was cloned or replayed, and it is terminated. The system trusts a knoll only after its actions survive the consistency check. From the walnut to the vertex, the same rule holds: no continuity, no trust, no exception.
